## Overview

This integration connects Gladys Assistant to the **Enki** cloud (the smart
home ecosystem sold by **Leroy Merlin** / Adeo) to control your Enki devices —
**lights, ceiling fans, outlets, roller shutters and sensors** — from Gladys,
using the same account as the Enki mobile app.

Once configured, every compatible device of your Enki account appears in the
Gladys **Discovery** screen. Depending on the device, it exposes these features:

- **Light** — turn the bulb (or the fan's light kit) on or off;
- **Brightness** — dim the light between 0 and 100 %, when the bulb is dimmable;
- **Color temperature** — warm-to-cold white, when the bulb is tunable-white;
- **Color** — RGB color, when the bulb supports it;
- **Fan speed** — the ceiling fan speed from 0 (off) to 100 % (Enki levels 1–6);
- **Airflow direction** — forward / reverse blade rotation, when supported;
- **Outlet** — on/off for connected sockets and relays;
- **Roller shutter** — position from 0 (closed) to 100 % (open), plus stop;
- **Sensors** — temperature, humidity, illuminance, motion, opening/contact,
  water leak and low-battery, when the device reports them;
- **Heating** — target temperature (radiators/thermostats) and pilot-wire mode
  (comfort / eco / frost-protection / off), plus the current temperature.

Detection is **capability-based**, so most Enki / Leroy Merlin models work
out of the box (around 150 of the ~210 catalogued models). A ceiling fan with a
light kit shows both the fan and the light features on the same device, and a
multisensor shows every reading it provides. States are refreshed every 15
seconds, so changes made from the Enki app or a physical remote show up in
Gladys shortly after.

Sirens, cameras and energy metering are not handled yet.

## Prerequisites

- An **Enki account** with your devices already **paired and visible in the Enki
  mobile app**. This integration does not replace Enki pairing: set the devices
  up in the Enki app first.
- Internet access from your Gladys instance: the integration talks to the Enki
  cloud, not to the devices directly.
- Only **Enki / Leroy Merlin** lights and ceiling fans are handled. Third-party
  Zigbee devices paired on the Enki hub are out of scope (use Zigbee2MQTT / ZHA).

## Configuration

1. Install the integration from the Gladys store.
2. Open its **Configuration** screen and fill in:
   - **Enki email** — the email address of your Enki account;
   - **Enki password** — the password of that account (stored as a secret,
     never displayed back).
3. Save. The integration logs in to Enki and loads your devices.
4. Open the **Discovery** screen: your lights and fans are listed there. Add the
   ones you want, then place them in your rooms and dashboards like any Gladys
   device.

To use another Enki account later, just update the email and password in the
Configuration screen: the integration reconnects and refreshes the device list
automatically.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Enki is not configured" during discovery** — the email or password is
  missing: fill in both fields in the Configuration screen and save.
- **Login fails** — double-check your credentials by signing in with the Enki
  mobile app.
- **A device is missing from Discovery** — make sure it is a Leroy Merlin / Enki
  light or ceiling fan and that it is visible in the Enki app with the same
  account, then run the discovery again.
- **Commands seem ignored** — the Enki cloud can take a few seconds to push a
  command to the device; the state in Gladys reflects the cloud state and
  catches up at the next 15-second poll.
- **States stop updating** — the Enki session may have expired; the integration
  refreshes its token automatically. If the problem persists, check the
  integration logs from its configuration page in Gladys.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Enki te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enki email | `string` | Sí | The email address of your Enki account (the one used in the Enki mobile app). |
| Enki password | `secret` | Sí | The password of your Enki account. |

## Cómo instalar Enki en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Enki aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/callemand/gladys-enki:1.0.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/callemand/gladys-enki](https://github.com/callemand/gladys-enki).

Enki requiere Gladys `>=4.62.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Enki es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [callemand](https://github.com/callemand), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
